item.description:
Arrive at 9:00 AM, 15 minutes before the start of the ride so that you will not keep your group waiting. Unfortunately Line 2 - Broadview to St. George will be closed until 11:00 AM! Alan Gordon Memorial Ride to Port Credit This is our longest ride of the year. Note the earlier start time. The ride is a memorial to Alan Gordon who, in 1995, created the Leisure Wheeler category, designed the rides and led them. In the year 2000 he and Eileen Harbinson designed a metric century for the Leisure Wheelers. This year, we have shortened the ride. The route will take us on the new Don Trail which skirts the beautiful new Biidaasige Park on the way to Cherry St. Bring a picnic lunch to eat by the lak...

item.description:

In this talk, you will learn how to identify hiring trends within the job market, pursue potential career paths, and how to interpret labour market data. Eddie is the founder and C.E.O of the consulting firm OneHub and has over thirty years of experience helping both employees and employers navigate the Canadian job market. Summer has to end eventually — so why not send it off properly? Join us on **Toronto Island** for an evening bonfire at Olympic Island as we say goodbye to summer and welcome the beginning of fall. We’ll take the ferry across together, settle in by the fire, enjoy some food and music, roast marshmallows, and spend the evening relaxing by the water with the Toronto skyline in the background.

item.title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Quand la représentation sociale cède la place aux sentiments. — Sat Oct 24, 2:00 PM
item.description: Du Néoclassicisme à l’Académisme, de David à Ingres, les commandes de portraits furent souvent le moyen d’affirmer son rang dans la société. Du Romantisme à l’Impressionnisme, une sensibilité nouvelle se fait jour : l’on pose en communion avec la nature et non plus dans la magnificence de sa demeure, les regards traduisent des sentiments (Renoir) et non plus une volonté de puissance, les gestes sont spontanés (Degas, Manet) et non plus codifiés. Quant aux artistes, ils valorisent, dans leurs autoportraits, l’acte créateur, l’inspiration (Girodet, Delacroix), voire les tourments intérieurs (Courbet, Baudelaire). Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’ Alliance française de Toronto . item.title: Botanical Drypoint Printmaking — Sat Oct 31, 1:00 PM — Toronto Botanical Garden
item.description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of drypoint printmaking! In this hands-on workshop, you’ll be creating an edition of 5 original prints using a printmaking technique called drypoint. This medium is similar to etching, but it’s far safer because no dangerous acids are involved. Rembrandt is a well known Old Master who excelled at both drypoint and etching.
For botanical subject matter, please bring sketches and line drawings for inspiration and reference. The image needs to measure 4×6 inches; you’ll learn how to incise the image onto a printing plate using a drypoint needle. If you’re stuck for ideas on what to create, there will be pressed leaves available which make lovely subjects. You’ll also learn how to ink the plate and work with an old-fashioned mechanical printing press.
Drypoint gets messy, so please wear old clothes or bring an apron. Also, please bring a pair of dishwashing gloves.
